scenarios.title: Pinch only with the declared cover
scenarios.objective: Evaluate a pinch under an explicitly stated cover assignment.
scenarios.briefing: Navy uses a drill rule: YOU may pinch the puck-side wall only while F3 covers your high position. F1 contests Gold 1’s rim; F3 is currently closer to Gold’s net than the puck, so the named cover is not established. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: F3 is deeper in the attacking zone than YOU, rather than occupying the high position.

questions.prompt: Is the stated high cover already established?

options.text: Yes; F3 has replaced YOU at the point
Yes; Gold 2 is Navy’s cover
No; F3 is currently closer to Gold’s net than YOU

questions.explanation: F3 is deeper in the attacking zone than YOU, rather than occupying the high position.

questions.prompt: Select two checks before acting on the pinch option.

options.text: Whether F3 can establish the agreed cover
The quality of the puck contest
Whether a rim always requires a pinch

questions.explanation: The source principle is conditional support; this exercise adds its own explicit cover rule.

questions.prompt: Arrange a supported-pinch decision.

options.text: Read the wall contest
Confirm the assigned high cover
Pinch or recover based on the updated picture

questions.explanation: The checks may overlap. Do not treat this drill’s cover rule as every team’s system.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a conservative high position while cover is uncertain.
questions.explanation: The reference retains access to central recovery rather than committing to the wall. Other high positions may work.

questions.prompt: F3 now reaches your vacated point and calls the switch. What changes?

options.text: The cover condition is met, but the puck contest still needs checking
The pinch becomes certain to win
Gold 1 no longer affects the decision

questions.explanation: A covered pinch can still lose a race or encounter a closed route.

questions.prompt: Explain what makes this a supported pinch rather than simply an aggressive move.
questions.explanation: Identify F3’s actual coverage, D2’s position and the puck situation; do not rely on the word “pinch” alone.

questions.prompt: F3 has not reached YOUR high position. Which call fits before a possible pinch?

options.text: F3, confirm high cover before I step down
D2 is on the ice, so I am going now
F1 is near the puck, so the cover can wait

questions.explanation: The drill names F3 as the replacement for YOUR high position. Ask for that cover and check the puck route before committing; a call alone does not establish it.

questions.prompt: After F3 reaches high cover, which changes would make YOU reconsider the pinch?

options.text: F3 leaves that high position
The puck moves beyond F1’s reachable route
Gold stays away from the puck

questions.explanation: The hypothetical cover is now established, but a change in cover or puck access can remove the reason to pinch. Hold or recover if the updated picture no longer supports it.

questions.prompt: Move F3 to illustrate the named replacement for YOUR high position.
questions.explanation: F3 is now near YOUR high area, on the neutral-zone side of the wall contest. This illustrates the cover condition; whether a pinch is reachable still needs a fresh puck read.

questions.prompt: F3 reaches YOUR high area, but the loose puck travels past F1 toward neutral ice. What changes?
questions.explanation: High cover satisfies only one condition. If YOU cannot reach the puck safely, hold or recover and communicate the escape route. F3 arriving does not make every pinch useful.

scenarios.title: Draw one penalty killer at the half wall
scenarios.objective: Recognize a local passing choice within a stated five-on-four setup.
scenarios.briefing: Navy has five skaters against four. YOU control the puck at the puck-side half wall. In this exercise F2 is the low option and F3 the slot option; Gold 1 is the nearest penalty killer. No named formation is mandatory. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The actor list and briefing specify five-on-four.

questions.prompt: What manpower advantage is explicitly shown?

options.text: An even three-on-three drill
Five Navy skaters against four Gold
Four Navy against five Gold

questions.explanation: The actor list and briefing specify five-on-four.

questions.prompt: Which two checks matter before moving the puck past Gold 1?

options.text: Which option Gold 1 closes
The assumption that the extra skater guarantees a seam
Whether the other receiver is ready

questions.explanation: An advantage still needs a usable route and receiver.

questions.prompt: Order a local power-play read.

options.text: Locate Gold 1 relative to both receivers
Observe which route pressure closes
Use or recreate an available connection

questions.explanation: This routine teaches a local read, not compulsory setup movements.

questions.prompt: Move YOU along the half wall to compare a new passing angle.
questions.explanation: The move changes the relation to F2 and F3. It is useful only if possession and routes remain available.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 commits down toward F2. Which option deserves a fresh check?

options.text: The same low pass without checking Gold 1
An automatic shot through Gold 2
The inside connection toward F3

questions.explanation: F3 may become more accessible, but Gold 2 and the actual seam still matter.

questions.prompt: Name your rink area and explain how changing the angle can affect two receivers.
questions.explanation: Use half wall, low support or slot accurately; describe the defender’s responsibility rather than assuming every option opens.

questions.prompt: What should YOU call before moving the puck?

options.text: Gold 1 is near the inside route; check F2 and F3
The power play removes all pressure
F2 is the next receiver regardless of Gold 1’s position

questions.explanation: Name the pressure and both possible receivers. Gold 1 is nearer the route to F3 than the direct route to F2 in this picture.

questions.prompt: Which two updates can make F3 the better option?

options.text: Gold 1 shifts toward F2
F3 keeps a reachable inside lane
The power-play label stays the same

questions.explanation: Coverage movement and lane access explain why F3 can become useful.

questions.prompt: Move YOU nearer the middle to compare a passing angle toward F3.
questions.explanation: The example changes the carrier’s angle to F2 and F3. Recheck the defenders and both receivers before choosing a pass.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 closes F3 instead. What should YOU re-read?
questions.explanation: Check F2, the wall lane, and whether protection preserves possession. The first angle does not decide the new branch.

scenarios.title: Replace high support after the entry pass
scenarios.objective: Track a changing support role after a delay pass.
scenarios.briefing: YOU delayed in a wide attacking-zone lane and passed inside to F2. Under the coach’s plan, YOU now offer support closer to the blue line than F2 as the attack continues. Navy attacks the right net.
cues: Under the coach’s plan, YOU now offer support closer to the blue line than F2 as the attack continues.

questions.prompt: Who carries the puck after the described pass?

options.text: Gold 3
F2 inside the zone
YOU at the wall

questions.explanation: The puck is assigned to F2; YOU are the passer in the stated rotation.

questions.prompt: Which two things matter when filling high support?

options.text: The space behind F2’s attack
A need to follow every pass directly to the net
D1’s existing position

questions.explanation: Support should replace a useful role without duplicating another player.

questions.prompt: Arrange the stated post-pass support change.

options.text: Confirm F2’s reception
Check the available high space
Reoffer high support behind the continuing attack

questions.explanation: The team-plan assumption is explicit; another system might keep the passer closer to Gold’s net.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a high-slot support example after the pass.
questions.explanation: This position changes from wall carrier to higher support. Avoid occupying D1’s exact point position.

questions.prompt: If F2 immediately loses the puck to Gold 2, what takes priority in your read?

options.text: Completing the offensive rotation without looking
Treating F2 as the carrier anyway
Whether high support can help the defensive transition

questions.explanation: A possession change can turn high support into useful defensive support.

questions.prompt: Name the space you filled and the option it leaves for F2.
questions.explanation: Describe high slot versus point and a possible return connection; do not treat those areas as interchangeable.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate after F2 receives?

options.text: I will offer high support; call if the lane changes
The entry guarantees a clean setup
F3 remains low even if the inside lane changes

questions.explanation: Communicate the planned high support after F2 receives. YOU still need to move and check the route; the call does not mean the position is already reached.

questions.prompt: Which two cues decide whether to stay high?

options.text: F2's puck control
Gold's inside pressure
The entry label alone

questions.explanation: Carrier control and pressure determine whether the high lane remains useful.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a high support point separated from F2.
questions.explanation: The example is closer to the blue line than F2. Check the passing route and leave room for F3 and D1.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 wins the puck. What responsibility changes first?
questions.explanation: Confirm Gold possession, then recover toward the dangerous lane. The former entry support job is no longer current.

scenarios.title: Hinge around a two-player forecheck
scenarios.objective: Assess a reset when the first forward lanes are covered.
scenarios.briefing: YOU control a neutral-zone regroup. Gold 1 closes your board side and Gold 2 screens the direct route to F1. D2 is deeper on the opposite side; the drill permits a D-to-D reset when available. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: D2 is closer to Navy’s net and on the opposite side of the rink.
YOU control a neutral-zone regroup. Gold 1 closes your board side and Gold 2 screens the direct route to F1. D2 is deeper on the opposite side; the drill permits a D-to-D reset when available.

questions.prompt: Which teammate is deeper and across the rink from YOU?

options.text: F1
F2
D2

questions.explanation: D2 is closer to Navy’s net and on the opposite side of the rink.

questions.prompt: Which two checks matter for the reset?

options.text: Whether D2 is prepared to receive
Whether Gold 1 can pressure its route
Whether the same reset worked earlier in the game

questions.explanation: The reset is a permitted option, not a guaranteed solution.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possible reset assessment.

options.text: Read the covered forward routes
Check D2 and the lateral connection
Reset or choose another available play

questions.explanation: After a reset, the new carrier must make a new read rather than replay the old one.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a different angle for the D-to-D option.
questions.explanation: A deeper angle can change Gold 1’s path to the puck. It may also cost time, so the pressure must be judged.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 leaves F1’s route to close on D2. What deserves attention?

options.text: Whether F1’s route has reopened
The reset regardless of Gold 2’s movement
An assumption that both routes are still equally covered

questions.explanation: Forecheckers changing jobs can alter the first option; reassess instead of committing mechanically.

questions.prompt: What makes a reset useful rather than merely moving the same problem to D2?
questions.explanation: D2 needs time, a controllable pass and a next option different from the pressure YOU face.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate during the regroup?

options.text: D2 is deeper; I will look for the connection that keeps pressure visible
The D-to-D pass is required
Gold 2 has stopped forechecking

questions.explanation: The message names D2 and makes the connection conditional on the changing forecheck.

questions.prompt: Which two changes can make the D-to-D option poor?

options.text: Gold 2 closes D2
F1 becomes a safer reachable outlet
Assuming every regroup requires the same reset

questions.explanation: Pressure and an alternative outlet decide whether the reset helps.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a different passing angle toward D2.
questions.explanation: The example moves the carrier closer to Gold 1 and farther from D2. Compare pressure and reach rather than assuming the new angle is safer.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 leaves F1 to close D2, but Gold 3 fills the lane. What should YOU re-read?
questions.explanation: Name Gold 3 as the new pressure and check F1, D2 and the protected side before choosing a pass.

scenarios.title: Replace the teammate who cycles below the goal line
scenarios.objective: Keep a useful high option when a forward moves low.
scenarios.briefing: F1 controls below the attacking goal line. F2 has moved down the side boards to support. YOU are arriving from the high slot. The exercise calls for one forward to remain higher than the puck as an outlet. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: Both F1 and F2 have greater x positions, deeper toward the attacking end.

F1 controls below the attacking goal line. F2 has moved down the side boards to support. YOU are arriving from the high slot. The exercise calls for one forward to remain higher than the puck as an outlet.

questions.prompt: Which two forwards are already deeper in Gold’s end than YOU?

options.text: F1 and F2
D1 and D2
Gold 1 and Gold 3

questions.explanation: Both F1 and F2 have greater x positions, deeper toward the attacking end.

questions.prompt: Which two checks help retain a high outlet?

options.text: Whether every forward should follow the puck low
F1’s ability to see out of pressure
Gold 2’s position in the middle

questions.explanation: The assigned high role creates another option but still needs a lane.

questions.prompt: Arrange a high-support read during this cycle.

options.text: Notice F2 joining low
Check the open high-slot pocket
Reoffer high support behind the puck

questions.explanation: The exercise defines the high role; actual timing should follow the carrier’s pressure.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a high-slot pocket separated from the two low forwards.
questions.explanation: The reference changes the lane around Gold 2 without joining the low cluster. Another high pocket may work.

questions.prompt: If F1 passes to YOU in that pocket, what should happen next?

options.text: Return the puck low without looking
Read the new pressure before choosing shot, pass or carry
Shoot automatically because YOU are high

questions.explanation: The support movement creates a new decision rather than a predetermined finish.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between the high slot and following F2 down the half wall.
questions.explanation: Use depth, passing angle and the team’s remaining support—not just the two area names.

questions.prompt: What should YOU call while F2 cycles below?

options.text: I am high; show me if F1 can use the outlet
The low cycle makes the high lane irrelevant
F1 is the preferred receiver even if the high lane closes

questions.explanation: The call preserves a high option while the low carrier changes.

questions.prompt: Which two cues support staying high?

options.text: F1 and F2 occupy different low spaces
The carrier can see a high outlet
The distance to the boards decides whether to stay high

questions.explanation: Separation and visibility explain the high support choice.

questions.prompt: If F2 receives a cycle pass behind the goal line, compare a new high support point.
questions.explanation: The example stays nearer the blue line than the low forwards. F2’s new position is hypothetical, so check the actual lane and Gold 2 before calling for a pass.

questions.prompt: F1 passes to YOU in the pocket. What should be scanned next?
questions.explanation: Check Gold coverage, F2's route, and the net-side lane before choosing a shot, pass, or reset.
